names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιοι Ηλίας, Πρόβος και Άρης», with the rank word left off. The page glosses the name itself, «(από το σανκριστικό mar = καταιγίδα) = ο θυελλώδης», and adds a note about the god of war of the myths, which is not about this saint.

death.note: saint.gr's name-block head for him alone, «Αγιος Αρης (; - 308)». The page's narrative gives no year for any of the three and no year of birth, and his two companions carry no year at all.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Ηλίας, Πρόβος και Άρης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. **The entry enumerates its company — three named men — so it is a folder each, and each relates the other two.** The page's whole narrative is two sentences: the holy Elias, Probus — or Promus, as it gives him a second name — and Ares came of Egypt, and inspired by their warm faith went about to various cities and served the persecuted Christians; at Ascalon they were arrested, held to their confession of Jesus Christ, and were condemned to death by the judge Firmilianus; Elias and Probus were beheaded and Ares gave up his holy soul in the flames. **Only Ares carries a year, and only in the page's name-block head, «Αγιος Αρης (; - 308)»; Elias and Probus carry none at all, and none is inferred for them from his.** It names Egypt and Ascalon and no coordinate is proposed. It prints no hymn. **An identity question named and not decided: saint.gr keeps an «Όσιος Άρης» on 13 Δεκεμβρίου too, one of the ascetics of the Egyptian desert whose sayings are in the Evergetinos, drafted in that day's batch as `ares-of-the-egyptian-desert`. Two entries on one calendar are two commemorations, and these two Ares are a desert elder who died in peace and a martyr burnt at Ascalon under Firmilianus; nothing is merged.**
